summary:
Podcast show notes for Episode 406 of Eptura's Workplace Innovator, hosted by Mike Petrusky, featuring Alexander Wennerberg, CEO and Founder of Hives.co, a platform focused on collecting and acting on employee ideas.

Core argument: innovation works best when the people closest to workplace problems are empowered to propose and implement solutions, rather than relying only on top-down initiatives. Wennerberg urges facility management and corporate real estate teams to make their "invisible" work more visible so they are recognized as value drivers instead of cost centers. This framing of proving FM value is the episode's central theme.

He also recommends treating workplaces as ongoing experiments, with continuous feedback gathered from the people who actually use the space rather than only from executives. On technology, he positions AI as a tool to organize and surface employee feedback, not to replace genuine human observation and lived experience, which he sees as the real driver of workplace progress.

On change management, the discussion stresses treating employees as active participants rather than passive recipients of change, which builds engagement and trust. The notes close with links to Wennerberg's LinkedIn, Hives.co, the YouTube playlist, Eptura resources, and Mike Petrusky's LinkedIn.

The item is promotional show-copy rather than reporting: it contains no statistics, survey data, or named case studies, and no discussion of specific workplace operations topics such as desk booking, visitor management, RTO mandates, or service desk metrics. Its value to a listening pipeline is as directional commentary on FM value narratives, employee-led innovation, feedback loops, and the appropriate role of AI in workplace experience programs.

claims.claim: Innovation is most effective when it empowers those closest to workplace problems to propose and implement solutions rather than relying solely on top-down initiatives.
Facility management and real estate teams should make their invisible work more visible so they are seen as value drivers rather than cost centers.
Organizations should treat workplaces as ongoing experiments, valuing continuous feedback from space users rather than just executives.
AI should be used to organize and surface employee feedback, not to replace genuine human observations and experiences.
Successful change management treats employees as active participants rather than passive recipients, encouraging engagement and trust.
